reachable: Yes, at the scored position, on all three axes. (arch) Built parent and child with the same manual_seed: all 109 inherited parameters are bit-identical and the forward output differs by exactly 0.0 everywhere, including at the read position — the "exactly the parent's function at init" claim is literal. On a scoring-shaped layout (cmd,obs,...,cmd with the read command alone, plus a shorter padded row), the fingerprint `code` at the read position is fully populated (norms 7.26 and 7.17 at the two rows' read commands; count = every prefix observation), so the "gated on an observation being present, therefore off at the read" failure mode does NOT apply here — the cumsums are shifted by one and read strictly-earlier observations, which all exist at the read. Backpropagating a loss taken ONLY at the two read positions gives comp_in.code_proj.weight a grad norm of 5.63 and variance_out.weight 4.60, so the coupling term is trained by exactly the position the score reads. (variance_down shows grad 0 only because variance_out is zero-init; variance_out gets gradient immediately and unblocks it after step 1.) The new parameters also do not disturb the optim's shape-based routing: (192,768) and (64,768) and (1536,64) all miss both the key_d and the (D,D) selectors. (objective/batcher) Both are training-time only; they act through what the net learns, not through the scored forward. A 25-step end-to-end run of the actual genome through harness._train on proxy-encoded real trajectories completes with a finite loss.
solves_outside_model: No. The batcher's command parsing is the legitimate kind. `_transport_mass` is called only inside `make_batcher`; `load_batcher` is referenced only in `evolve/harness.py:78` and `eval/smoke.py` — never in cups_probe, cups_ca or the adapter's measurement path. It returns a float per sequence that is used solely as an Efraimidis-Spirakis sampling weight over indices; the tokens the model sees are the untouched cmd/obs embeddings of whichever sequences got picked, and `fit` is verified unmutated after 3000 steps. This is "parse commands to choose SAMPLES", explicitly allowed. The objective sees only (pred, tgt), declares no WANTS_CTX, and gets no command side-channel; its equivalence classes are computed from target-target distances alone. The arch's fingerprint reads only tok_emb[:, 1::2] (observations); the role-swap re-encodes command tokens at even positions only (cups_probe writes `tok[i, 2*j] = z[j]`), so `code` is bit-identical in the native and swapped arms and cannot by itself manufacture a native-minus-swap difference. No resolved routing reaches the model as input at scoring time. The prior-retraction shape is absent.
summary: The code does what the hypothesis says, and the load-bearing measured numbers reproduce exactly. Data claims: 262/724 empty observations (36.19%) — exact; per-sequence transport mass 4..36, mean 12.5 — exact. Objective: with all targets distinct, r4_dupclass_ring_negatives returns a value with absolute difference 0.0 from r12_antiretrieval_ring_negatives, and a diff shows every other term is byte-for-byte the parent's; with a clique of 20 identical targets and a perfect prediction, the parent's per-row NLL is 2.81 (log 20 = 3.00) with focal 0.94, the child's is 0.0096 with focal 0.0096 — the "irreducible floor that is also focal-up-weighted" is real and is removed, exactly as claimed. On a realistic batch (64 sequences, 1954 rows) the largest coincident class is 722 rows, matching the predicted ~700 of ~1900. Batcher: over 3000 steps with n=1440, bs=64, zero batches contained a duplicate index; the parent's batcher produced a duplicate in 2922 of 3000 — claim (a) is verified and the parent's defect is real. The transport tilt is real and well-targeted: mass >= 12 holds for exactly the 12 of 24 sequences containing a >=3-hop read and mass <= 8 for the other 12 (Pearson 0.80 against deep-read count); realized pick frequency runs ~36 to ~115 across the mass range. The sampler is deterministic, uses a private generator, is unaffected by the global RNG, and does not mutate fit. Arch: init bit-identity to the parent is exact (max |diff| = 0.0), the fingerprint is live at the read, and the crossover is genuinely coupled rather than stacked — code_proj adds into comp_in's pre-activation inside the renderer's hidden layer and receives gradient from a read-position-only loss. The two claims the author flagged as unmeasured are now measured and negligible: batcher 0.045 ms/step vs the parent's 0.020 ms; arch fwd+bwd 708.6 ms vs 706.1 ms (+0.4%). The author's self-declared sharpest risk (1e-3 collapsing genuine foils) does not materialize on a proxy encoder: distinct canary observations sit at tt = 0.128, 128x above the threshold. All four divergences are minor and none of them flatter the mechanism — the render_obs error understates the clique, and the stated hop histogram is a stale hand-count that contradicts the author's own mean while the number the code actually uses reproduces exactly. What I could NOT check: (1) the real training split size, so the "distinct whenever len(fit) > bs" precondition and the degenerate len(fit) <= 64 fallback are untested against the actual pack; (2) the real fine-tuned eye (TJ_FT_ENCODER is unset and the pack roots are not on this machine) — all tt geometry above is intfloat/e5-base-v2 with the correct nocwd render but standardized on the 24-sequence sample rather than the pack frame; (3) whether coincident class sizes stay moderate for NON-empty observations on the real diverse split — my end-to-end batch replicated 24 sequences, which overstates duplication; (4) whether any of this actually moves comp_ca.

divergences.claim: "render_obs turns such a step into exactly one of two strings, 'cwd=/ exit=0\n' or 'cwd=/data exit=0\n'" — i.e. the 262 empty-output rows form TWO identical-target classes (227 + 35).
divergences.what_the_code_does: The author quoted realenv/seq_worldmodel.render_obs, but the encode is done by the perception impl the eye names. The default eye is enc_e5_ft_nocwd_hf, which re-exports enc_e5_base_nocwd.render_obs = f"passage: exit={exit}\n{out}" — cwd is dropped. All 262 empty-output steps render to the SINGLE string 'passage: exit=0\n'. The claim's count (262/724 = 36.19%) is exactly right; the 'two strings' detail is wrong, in the direction that makes the clique bigger and the proposal's premise stronger.

divergences.claim: "the sampler is exactly uniform-without-replacement at step 1".
divergences.what_the_code_does: r = min(1.0, step/ramp_steps) is 1/ramp_steps at step 1, not 0, so w = base_w**(chain_alpha*r) is not identically 1. With steps=4000 and ramp_frac=0.3, r = 1/1200 and the most-tilted sequence's weight is 1.0012 rather than 1.0 — uniform to within 0.12%, not exactly uniform.
divergences.evidence: batcher line 72-73: r = min(1.0, float(step)/float(ramp_steps)); w = base_w.pow(chain_alpha*r). Measured: r at step1 = 0.001111, base_w range [0.32, 2.88], max weight at step 1 = 1.00118.

divergences.claim: "float32 cancellation error for a genuinely identical pair lands near 1e-7 ... 1e-3 buys ~4 orders of magnitude of margin".
divergences.what_the_code_does: On a proxy encoder the largest tt between two rows carrying identical observation TEXT is 3.8e-6, not ~1e-7 — still 2.4 orders below the 1e-3 threshold, so the conclusion holds but the stated margin is ~1.5 orders optimistic. On the foil side, the closest pair of DISTINCT canary observations sits at tt = 0.128, 128x above the threshold; the only false merges in the whole corpus are trailing-whitespace variants of the same 'total 0' output, which are the same observation.
